official.tuition_coverage_note: The official pages describe the award only as supplementary financial assistance paid to the recipient and do not state that tuition fees are covered.

benefits: Supplementary financial assistance up to a maximum amount of AUD $75,000
Paid directly to the recipient in equal instalments at the start of each semester or term, subject to academic progress

Administered by the Aurora Education Foundation and jointly funded by the Australian Government (National Indigenous Australians Agency), the British High Commission (Chevening), Cambridge Australia Scholarships Ltd, Cambridge Commonwealth Trust and the University of Cambridge
On returning to Australia, Roberta Sykes Scholars are strongly encouraged to give back to their communities
eligibility: Be of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent, identify as an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander and be accepted as such by the community in which you live or have lived, with written confirmation from an incorporated Indigenous organisation or Land Council
Provide written confirmation of enrolment in a postgraduate course at an overseas institution
Provide a budget outlining how the scholarship funds will be used, including all additional funding and income
Demonstrate how your chosen course of study will support you in contributing to your community and the wider Indigenous community upon your return to Australia

Full-time study at doctoral research, postgraduate coursework or postgraduate research level, in any area of study, at a recognised overseas university; listed institutions are Cambridge, Harvard, New York University (NYU), Oxford, University College London and Other
Open to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students only
requirements: Submit an application with all required documents by the Scholarship closing date; applications without all required documents will not be considered complete or pass the shortlisting process
Written confirmation of full-time enrolment from the relevant university, or written confirmation of the application submitted to the relevant university
Ensure all references are emailed by the referee directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au
Academic references must be from academic staff such as Lecturers, Tutors and Course Coordinators; professional staff such as Student Success Officers will not be accepted
Professional references must be from someone who is or was your reporting manager
documents: Personal statement of no more than two pages covering why you want to study your chosen course, how you identify with and have contributed to Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander community/communities, and how completing the course will tangibly advance the aspirations of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and communities
Written confirmation of full-time enrolment from the relevant university, or written confirmation of the application submitted to it
Current Curriculum Vitae (CV), most up-to-date official academic transcript, and a high-resolution corporate headshot in jpeg format

Confirmation of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander identity: a letter stamped with the common seal and signed by the chairperson of an Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Land Council in whose area you live or have previously lived, or a letter stamped and signed by an authorised delegate of an incorporated Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander organisation
Completed budget using the downloadable template within the application form

References emailed by the referee directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au: one written reference from an Elder or senior member of your community, plus two written academic references or one academic and one professional written reference
selection_criteria: Commitment to contributing to improving outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities
Demonstration of how the chosen course of study will support contributions to your community and the wider Indigenous community upon return to Australia
Completeness of the application by the closing date, as applications missing required documents do not pass shortlisting
coverage: Supplementary financial assistance of up to a maximum amount of AUD $75,000
Paid directly to the recipient in equal instalments at the start of each semester or term, subject to academic progress
Applicants must provide a budget outlining how the scholarship funds will be used, including all additional funding and income
application_method: Open the Roberta Sykes Scholarship listing on Aurora's Indigenous Pathways Portal and select the More & apply function, which opens the application portal at banksia.aurorafoundation.com.au
Sign in or sign up for an Aurora Indigenous Pathways Portal profile, complete the application form and upload all required documents
Instruct referees to email their references directly to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au
Contact Aurora's Pathways Scholarships team at scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au if you are unable to obtain a Confirmation of Aboriginality
official.application_route: Apply online through the Aurora Indigenous Pathways Portal (sign in or sign up, open the Roberta Sykes Scholarship listing and select More & apply), submitting all required documents by the 29 January 2027 close.
official.citizenship_residency: Open to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students only; applicants must be of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander descent, identify as an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander and be accepted as such by the community in which they live or have lived.
official.international_eligibility: Not open to international students generally: the published rule is 'Open to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Students Only', with study undertaken at a recognised overseas university.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any area of study; no field restriction published. Study must be at a recognised overseas university, with the portal listing Cambridge, Harvard, New York University (NYU), Oxford, University College London and an Other option.
official.duration: Paid in equal instalments at the start of each semester or term, subject to academic progress
official.description: The Roberta Sykes Scholarship provides supplementary financial assistance to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander postgraduate students who wish to undertake full-time studies at any recognised overseas university. Roberta Sykes scholars must embody academic excellence and demonstrate a commitment to contributing to improving outcomes for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities. On their return to Australia, Roberta Sykes Scholars are strongly encouraged to give back to their communities.
official.region: Overseas (study at a recognised overseas university); Aurora Education Foundation, Australia
official.program_type: Postgraduate scholarship for overseas study administered by the Aurora Education Foundation through its Indigenous Pathways Portal

verification.notes: Amount (up to AUD $75,000 maximum), instalment schedule, funders, eligibility, document list and the 5 October 2026 to 29 January 2027 open/close dates were read directly from the Aurora Education Foundation's own scholarship detail page and its Study Tour and Scholarships page. Aurora does not publish whether the funds cover tuition, living or travel costs and publishes no English language or research proposal requirement, so those fields are null; tuition_coverage is recorded false because the award is officially framed as supplementary financial assistance rather than a full-cost award.

applicant_utility.summary: Aurora's Roberta Sykes Scholarship pays up to AUD 75,000 in total, straight to an Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander postgraduate enrolled full time at a recognised overseas university, released in equal instalments at the start of each semester or term once academic progress is confirmed. Because the award is officially 'supplementary', plan a broader funding package that still covers overseas tuition and living costs, and start the Confirmation of Aboriginality process first because Aurora marks any application without that document incomplete and does not assess it. The current round ran from 5 October 2026 to 29 January 2027, so aim to have enrolment evidence and referees locked in well before the close.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander postgraduates who hold a place, or have submitted an application, for full-time doctoral, coursework or research study overseas and can evidence academic strength plus a concrete record of community contribution.
application_readiness_checklist: Request the Confirmation of Aboriginality from your Land Council or incorporated Indigenous organisation immediately; it needs the common seal and the chairperson's (or authorised delegate's) signature and lead times run to weeks
Brief two academic referees (or one academic plus one professional manager) early and confirm they will send references from their own email to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au before the close
Secure an Elder or senior community member willing to write about your community connection and contributions
Open Aurora's downloadable budget template inside the application form and map every other income and funding source into it before you start writing
Assemble a current CV, your latest official academic transcript and a high-resolution jpeg corporate headshot before opening the form
Obtain written confirmation of full-time enrolment, or of your submitted university application, from the overseas institution
common_rejection_risks: No Confirmation of Aboriginality: Aurora states plainly that applications without this document are marked incomplete and will not be assessed
References forwarded by you instead of sent by the referee, or supplied by non-academic staff such as Student Success Officers, which Aurora explicitly does not accept
A personal statement that runs past two pages or omits one of the three required threads: course motivation, community identification and contribution, and tangible community benefit on return
Neither an enrolment confirmation nor proof that the university application was submitted
Incomplete document set at the closing date, since Aurora will not treat the application as complete or let it through shortlisting
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Overseas tuition plus any airfares, visas, insurance and living expenses above the AUD 75,000 ceiling: Aurora publishes no tuition, travel or living-cost coverage for this award, so those must come from university funding, other scholarships or personal income, and your budget must show them.
document_audit: The Confirmation of Aboriginality must carry the organisation's common seal; an unstamped, emailed verbal or unsigned confirmation fails
References must arrive from the referee's own email address to scholarships@aurorafoundation.com.au; copies you upload or forward can be treated as missing
An academic reference must come from lecturing or course staff (Lecturer, Tutor, Course Coordinator); administrative or student-success staff do not qualify
The personal statement is capped at two pages, so address the three required threads explicitly rather than narratively
The headshot must be a high-resolution jpeg; compressed phone screenshots often fail presentation quality
If you only have a submitted application rather than an offer, the university's written confirmation must say so clearly
alerts: The round closed 29 January 2027 after opening 5 October 2026; documents not submitted by that date make the application incomplete and ineligible for shortlisting
Aurora lists Cambridge, Harvard, NYU, Oxford, UCL and 'Other'; if your institution sits under Other you should be ready to show it is a recognised overseas university
Instalments are released per semester or term and are contingent on academic progress, so an enrolment interruption can pause payments

Do not confuse this with the Roberta Sykes Fellowship (up to AUD 30,000 for overseas research within an Australian program), the Roberta Sykes Executive Scholarship (up to AUD 20,000 for short executive courses, often with employer contribution), or the Chief Executive Women / Harvard Kennedy School award; the portal treats each as a separate round
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Create or log into your Aurora Indigenous Pathways Portal profile, open the Roberta Sykes Scholarship listing, select More & apply, upload every document into the form, and have referees email their references directly to Aurora before the 29 January 2027 close.
